- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 1–3% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp spike in price, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If official event net is bearish (supply net < 0) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model often underestimates downside; add 2–5% downward bias to forecast.  
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model tends to overestimate volatility; cap forecast range within ±3% of recent 7-day mean to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish swings, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply slight downward bias in 3rd–5th day of forecast horizon.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.5) and model is flat, force a 2–5% downward adjustment to reflect bearish sentiment persistence.
